newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: INTERVIEW-BT targets 4 bln stg/yr Asia sales.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-BT targets 4 bln stg/yr Asia sales.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc (BT) said on Tuesday it planned a major expansion across the Asia-Pacific which would bring its turnover in the region to around four billion pounds sterling by the year 2000.

Mike Burgess, director of strategy and joint ventures for BT-Asia Pacific, told Reuters the company expected that it and its partners would invest about four billion pounds in the Asia-Pacific region over the next three to four years.

"By 2000, we expect revenue of about four billion pounds a year from the Asia Pacific region," Burgess said in an interview. He added that an exact geographic breakdown was extremely difficult to estimate because revenue streams crossed national and regional barriers.
Burgess declined to give an estimate of BT's current annual Asia-Pacific revenue but analysts have put it at around one billion pounds a year.
BT's global turnover was 14.73 billion pounds in 1996.

"BT recognises that to achieve revenue of four billion pounds, something of the order of four billion in investments in the region would not be unreasonable, either directly by BT or by BT and its partners," he said.
BT is in the process of merging with the United States' second biggest telephone company MCI Communications Corp to form Concert Plc.
